title: Cocycle identity for the iterated Weil isomorphism
statement:
Let $(K,\varphi)\in D^b_{ctf,\mathrm W}(X,A)$ be a
strict Weil complex under the
conventions of [def-trf-strict-weil-complex], with
$g_\gamma=g_X$ the
geometric-Frobenius automorphism
of [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], and let

$$
\varphi^{[m]}:Lg_\gamma^{m*}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K
\qquad(m\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1})
$$

be the iterated Weil isomorphism
of [def-trf-iterated-weil-map]. Then for all
$m,n\in\mathbf Z_{\geq1}$ the identity

$$
\varphi^{[m+n]}=\varphi^{[m]}\circ Lg_\gamma^{m*}\varphi^{[n]}
$$

holds after the canonical pullback identifications
$Lg_\gamma^{m*}Lg_\gamma^{n*}K\cong L(g_\gamma^m\circ g_\gamma^n)^*K=Lg_\gamma^{m+n*}K$.

proof.text:
By [def-trf-strict-weil-complex], $\varphi:Lg_\gamma^*K\to K$ is an isomorphism in the underlying derived category of pro-etale $A$-modules. By [def-trf-scheme-frobenius], $g=g_\gamma$ is an automorphism. By [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], $A$ denotes the constant coefficient sheaf, so all powers of $g$ preserve it with the canonical identifications. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] to $h=g^m$, $k=g^n$: its natural comparison is $L(g^{m+n})^*\cong L(g^m)^*L(g^n)^*$. Put $F=Lg^*$ and identify $L(g^r)^*$ with the parenthesized iterate $F^r$ by repeated such comparisons. These identifications are natural on every derived morphism, since the comparison is an isomorphism of functors, not just an objectwise isomorphism.

Here is the coherence check needed when regrouping powers. For an arbitrary input derived object, take a representing complex and a K-flat resolution with flat terms by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], on the small pro-etale site with its constant commutative ring sheaf $A$. The computation clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition] identifies each comparison on this representative with its ordinary termwise comparison; that same clause says successive pullbacks of this representative remain K-flat with flat terms. In the identified-coefficient case [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] defines derived pullback by the exact module pullback applied termwise. After cancelling extension of scalars along the coefficient isomorphism, this is the inverse-image functor on underlying modules. Its ordinary composition identifications associate by identifying the same successive inverse images; equivalently, in the tensor presentations the two ways to expand three pullbacks both send a generator $v\otimes a$ to $((v\otimes1)\otimes1)\otimes a$. Tensor balancing and associativity of scalar multiplication give the same inverse in both cases. Thus these are equal maps in each degree on that representative, commute with differentials and localize to equal maps in the derived category. Every derived object admits the chosen representative, so this proves the required associativity for the canonical comparisons on all objects. Consequently regrouping the iterates, and mapping a morphism under them, uses compatible identifications. We may henceforth calculate with $F^mF^n=F^{m+n}$ and $F^0=\mathrm{id}$ in this notation.

proof.text:
For $i\geq0$ put

$$
a_i=F^i(\varphi):F^{i+1}K\longrightarrow F^iK.
$$

The definition [def-trf-iterated-weil-map] gives $\varphi^{[r]}=a_0\circ\cdots\circ a_{r-1}$ for every $r\geq1$ (a single factor when $r=1$). Functoriality of $F^m$ gives

$$
F^m(\varphi^{[n]})
=F^m(a_0)\circ\cdots\circ F^m(a_{n-1})
=a_m\circ\cdots\circ a_{m+n-1},
$$

since $F^m(F^j(\varphi))=F^{m+j}(\varphi)$ for $0\leq j<n$. The naturality and associativity verified in step 1 justify precisely these power identifications on each factor. Thus associativity of composition gives

$$
\varphi^{[m]}\circ Lg_\gamma^{m*}\varphi^{[n]}
=(a_0\circ\cdots\circ a_{m-1})\circ(a_m\circ\cdots\circ a_{m+n-1})
=a_0\circ\cdots\circ a_{m+n-1}
=\varphi^{[m+n]}.
$$

Every factor has the displayed source and target; in particular the last arrow toward $K$ is $a_0=\varphi:FK\to K$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q91-f1600e319 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery in full. It has one commit with the item and the report, and no new nodes. The item statement is identical to the blueprint in both the master (order 2297) and main-20261015 (order 2641) snapshots. All hypotheses are kept: the strict pair in D^b_ctf,W(X,A_{E,n}) on the small pro-etale site, the geometric-Galois g_gamma rather than the scheme Frobenius, m,n>=1, and the identity holding after the canonical comparisons. The type check holds: c_{h,k}: L(kh)^* -> Lh^*Lk^* with h=g^m, k=g^n, and g^n g^m = g^m g^n. Step 1 is correctly marked non-elementary. Its pair clause comes from def-trf-strict-weil-complex and the automorphism from def-trf-scheme-frobenius, both checked with their blueprint_update. def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom supplies the constant sheaf and termwise pullback. The coefficient identifications are compatible because each c_u in prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map is the unique map preserving constant sections. lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition (read with Stacks 0D6D, sites-cohomology.tex l.3657, statement and proof) gives the natural isomorphism, termwise on K-flat complexes with flat terms, and says pullback preserves that class. lem-pc-kflat-resolution (Stacks 06YS) gives such a resolution for every complex, with no boundedness hypothesis. def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations supplies termwise exact pullback and cancellation of scalar extension. The triple-comparison associativity is written out at generator level; it is the routine coherence of inverse images and not a hidden theorem. Step 2 is elementary: with a_i = F^i(phi): F^{i+1}K -> F^iK, def-trf-iterated-weil-map gives phi^[r] = a_0...a_{r-1}, applying F^m shifts the second block to a_m..a_{m+n-1}, and concatenation gives phi^[m+n]. The documented source error is genuine: the blueprint's final arrow is phi, not Lg^*phi. Edge cases checked: m=n=1, single-factor first or second block, m=n=2, K=0, X empty, and a scalar automorphism T on the point (T^{m+n} = T^m T^n). There is no cycle: the forward reference is only a pointer, and no dependency reaches back to the item. No duplicate exists; the Picard-framework coherence lemmas are for Zariski O_X-modules and the two trf neighbours concern R Gamma_c transport and traces.
